full_text_en:
Beijing Paris Damofang Food Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Sun City Shopping Center — trademark infringement dispute

Plaintiff: Beijing Paris Damofang Food Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Wei Lixin, Vice Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Hao Xiaofeng, Instructor, Department of Law, Peking University.

Defendant: Beijing Sun City Shopping Center.

Legal Representative: Yang Fuchang, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ping, Deputy General Manager of the Shopping Center.

Agent ad litem: Miao Xiuzhen, Attorney, Beijing No. 4 Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Beijing Paris Damofang Food Co., Ltd., filed an action with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Beijing Sun City Shopping Center, on the ground of trademark infringement.

The plaintiff, Beijing Paris Damofang Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Damofang Company), alleged that the plaintiff is the owner of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Damofang," the designated goods of which are bread. In October 1992, the plaintiff entered into a consignment sales agreement with the defendant, Beijing Sun City Shopping Center (hereinafter referred to as Sun City Shopping Center), stipulating that the defendant's food department would set up a consignment counter to be responsible for selling the plaintiff's bread. After supplying goods to the defendant until late April 1993, the plaintiff ceased further supply. However, starting from May 11 of the same year, the defendant used the registered trademark "Damofang" to sell bread purchased from other manufacturers that had the same appearance as the bread produced by the plaintiff, thereby infringing upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to cease the infringement, compensate for the infringement losses of over RMB 110,000, publicly apologize in the newspaper, and eliminate the adverse effects.

The defendant, Sun City Shopping Center, argued that although there was a contractual agreement between the parties, the bread supplied by the plaintiff was unpackaged and each piece of bread did not bear the trademark; the defendant had no intent to infringe and did not constitute infringement; the amount of compensation for losses claimed by the plaintiff was unsupported by evidence, and the defendant did not agree with the plaintiff's claims.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court, upon trial, found the following facts: On January 10, 1991, upon approval by the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, the plaintiff obtained the exclusive right to use the trademark "Damofang," with the designated goods being bread. In October 1992, Damofang Company entered into a consignment sales agreement for bread with the defendant, Sun City Shopping Center. The agreement stipulated that the defendant would set up a "Damofang" counter to sell bread produced by the plaintiff. The plaintiff was required to supply registered trademark goods that were famous, high-quality, special, and novel. After the contract was signed, no disputes arose between the parties during its performance. Starting from April 24, 1993, the plaintiff no longer supplied goods to the defendant. On June 8 of the same year, the plaintiff's agent went to the defendant's premises to inspect and found that at the "Damofang" bread counter set up by the defendant for the consignment sale of the plaintiff's products, bread with the same appearance as Damofang bread was still being sold, and the price tags indicated the place of origin as Damofang. The plaintiff then requested the Beijing Chongwen District Notary Public Office to question Zhang Xinping, the head of the defendant's boxed food department, and made on-site records, took photographs of the bread displayed at the counter, and conducted three notarizations, including the plaintiff's agent's purchase of bread from the "Damofang" counter. The defendant admitted that starting from May 11, 1993, it purchased bread with the same appearance as the bread produced by the plaintiff from a factory claiming to be a subordinate of Damofang Company. The purchase price of this batch of bread was RMB 765.55, and the profit earned was RMB 111.66. The plaintiff incurred the following expenses for evidence collection and filing the lawsuit: notarization fee of RMB 1,020, litigation agency fee of RMB 2,000, and round-trip car rental fee of RMB 1,538.60.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the agreement signed by both parties, the notarization documents, various receipts, invoices, and the statements of the parties.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court held that the plaintiff, Damofang Company, lawfully obtained the exclusive right to use the trademark "Damofang," with the designated goods being bread. The defendant, Sun City Shopping Center, without the plaintiff's permission, used the "Damofang" bread counter set up for the plaintiff's products to sell bread from other manufacturers that had the same appearance as "Damofang" bread. This was sufficient to cause consumers to confuse bread produced by different manufacturers, leading to consumer mispurchase, and harmed the interests of the plaintiff, who owns the exclusive right to use the trademark. Its conduct violated the provisions of Article 38, Item 1, of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China and constituted infringement. The defendant's argument that it had no intent to infringe and that the bread supplied by the plaintiff did not bear the registered trademark and was unpackaged food, thereby denying its infringement, was untenable. The trademark owner has the freedom to choose the method of using the trademark. The plaintiff's complaint had sufficient evidence and justified grounds, which should be supported. For the damage caused to the plaintiff's economic interests and commercial reputation by the defendant's infringing conduct, in accordance with Article 118 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that citizens and legal persons whose exclusive right to use a trademark is infringed have the right to demand cessation of the infringement, elimination of adverse effects, and compensation for losses, appropriate compensation should be given to the plaintiff. However, given that the plaintiff did not have sufficient facts to prove that the defendant's infringing conduct had caused it serious damage, the court could not grant the plaintiff's claims for an excessively high amount of compensation and for a public apology and elimination of adverse effects in newspapers. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment on October 30, 1993:

1. The defendant, Sun City Shopping Center, shall, from the date this judgment takes effect, cease its infringement of the plaintiff Damofang Company's exclusive right to use the trademark, and shall not engage in any similar infringing conduct in the future.

2. The defendant, Sun City Shopping Center, shall, within 10 days from the date this judgment takes effect, pay in a single lump sum to the plaintiff Damofang Company compensation for infringement losses in the amount of RMB 14,897.21 (including attorney's fees of RMB 2,000, investigation and evidence collection fees of RMB 2,020, the cost of the infringing food products of RMB 765.55 and the profit of RMB 111.66, and compensation for loss of trademark reputation of RMB 10,000).

3. All other claims of the plaintiff and the defendant are dismissed.

The litigation costs of this case, RMB 595.89, shall be borne by the defendant, Sun City Shopping Center.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appealed.
